introduction: Generated from [reviewed configuration](../../config/capability-inventory.config.json). Run `pnpm generate:capabilities` after reviewing claims; `pnpm check:capabilities` rejects drift and is part of `pnpm verify`.

Baseline: upstream [v0.3.0](https://github.com/shepherd-agents/shepherd/tree/a8196d4c453514836d06bd2fece91a03cdc37107) and [paper v3](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.10913v3), reviewed for issue #236. Release vocabulary, research targets, imported proof evidence and native extensions are distinct sections.

The gate checks emitted public exports, complete evidence dimensions, and SHA-256 pins of cited local files. It does not run cited experiments or establish that prose is true. Evidence pins require human review when their content changes; generation never refreshes them. Test files specify executable evidence, not passing live/platform results. No aggregate coverage percentage is assigned.
See [inventory maintenance](../capability-inventory.md) for verification commands and the review boundary.

rows.title: Typed tasks and explicit execution
rows.source: Upstream 0.3.0 task/schema vocabulary; adapted to explicit TypeScript descriptors and providers.

dimensions.api: Supported: scalar forms, arrays, literals/enums, disjoint unions, strict objects with optional fields, task values and whole-value void.
dimensions.composition: Adapted: explicit provider execution; no ambient Python decorator calls. General constraints, tuple/dictionary/recursive forms remain unsupported.
dimensions.recovery: Durable run reconstruction exists; a started uncertain provider operation is refused rather than blindly repeated.
dimensions.live: No live-provider result claimed; ordinary tests use deterministic providers.
dimensions.performance: No performance result claimed by this row.
dimensions.platforms: Node runtime support applies; filesystem/native support depends on the separately documented host and backend.
dimensions.formal: Runtime behavior only; no production correctness theorem claimed.

rows.title: Retained outputs, bindings and grants

dimensions.api: Supported: retained capture, inspect, select/apply/discard/release and authenticated repository grants.
dimensions.composition: Adapted: disjoint bindings can be created, but each retained task exposes one repository world. Built-in world operations do not each have an individual durable effect record. CLI task inspection does not expose grant evidence.
dimensions.recovery: Capture and settlement have durable recovery; this does not imply automatic safe tool-effect replay.
dimensions.live: No live-provider result claimed; ordinary tests use deterministic providers.
dimensions.performance: No performance result claimed by this row.
dimensions.platforms: Node runtime support applies; filesystem/native support depends on the separately documented host and backend.
dimensions.formal: Runtime behavior only; no production correctness theorem claimed.

rows.title: HTTP providers and process-provider boundary
rows.source: Upstream 0.3.0 provider concept: HTTP adapters are an adapted transport, not Claude CLI or Codex process adapters.

dimensions.api: Supported: Anthropic Messages and OpenAI-compatible HTTP adapters with tool blocks and cache-token usage.
dimensions.composition: Partial: no streaming, bounded retry policy, actual monetary accounting, or governed process-provider adapter.
dimensions.recovery: Conversation checkpoints are process-local; retained trace data does not reconstruct the checkpoint receipt map after restart.
dimensions.live: Opt-in live test exists but was not run in the recorded audit; no live cache-hit or tool-loop conformance result.
dimensions.performance: No performance result claimed by this row.
dimensions.platforms: Node runtime support applies; filesystem/native support depends on the separately documented host and backend.

rows.title: Tasks as substitutable values
rows.source: Paper §3.1: task values, substitution, revision, synthesis and nested meta-agents.

dimensions.api: Supported: canonical task values, explicit child-run handles and task provenance.
dimensions.composition: Adapted: revised and synthesized task values are data with approval gating; program-serviced children compose bounded nested agents. No ambient Python call semantics.
dimensions.recovery: Retained child identity, approval and completion records survive reopen/import; uncertain running children require the documented cancellation/retry path.
dimensions.live: No live synthesis or nested-agent experiment measured.
dimensions.platforms: Node runtime support applies; nested worlds inherit their carrier and placement limits.
dimensions.formal: Runtime authority/isolation tests; no production correctness theorem claimed.

rows.title: Effects, observation and interception

dimensions.composition: Adapted: in-process handler stacks alone are not durable dispatch. Direct retained-world operations still need per-operation effect integration.
dimensions.recovery: Subscriptions retain acknowledgements; supervised dispatch fences ownership. Neither proves all built-in world operations are journaled.
dimensions.live: No live-provider result claimed; ordinary tests use deterministic providers.
dimensions.performance: No performance result claimed by this row.
dimensions.platforms: Node runtime support applies; filesystem/native support depends on the separately documented host and backend.

dimensions.recovery: Trace inspection preserves claim boundaries across reopen/import; no process-state proof follows.
dimensions.live: No live-provider result claimed; ordinary tests use deterministic providers.
dimensions.performance: No performance result claimed by this row.
dimensions.platforms: Node runtime support applies; filesystem/native support depends on the separately documented host and backend.
dimensions.formal: Core-0/Core-A stronger reference claims depend on exact pinned artifacts. Core-0H is fail-closed without a trusted sidecar. External proof build remains unexecuted here.
